{
  "verdict": "fix",
  "issues": [
    "The GET /tasks endpoint omits pagination and filtering, which will cause severe performance and memory issues as the dataset grows.",
    "The PUT /tasks/{id} endpoint defines all body fields as optional. In REST, PUT implies a full resource replacement; partial updates should use PATCH to prevent accidental data nullification.",
    "The API contract completely lacks error response definitions (e.g., 400, 404, 500 status codes and error payload schemas), leaving clients without a standardized way to handle failures.",
    "Replacing OpenAPI with a custom JSON specification sacrifices industry-standard tooling (client generation, mock servers, validation) and forces developers to learn a proprietary format."
  ],
  "suggestions": [
    "Add pagination parameters (e.g., limit, offset, or cursor) to the GET /tasks endpoint to ensure scalability.",
    "Change the partial update endpoint to use the PATCH method, or explicitly define PUT as a full replacement where all fields are required.",
    "Define standard error response schemas and include common error status codes (400, 401, 404, 500) in the contract.",
    "Adopt the OpenAPI specification instead of a custom format to leverage existing ecosystem tools and reduce onboarding friction for API consumers."
  ]
}
